text:
maya: Heads-up — sample-app fails when run in Cloudflare Workers (edge) with our SDK ESM build. Types not picked up in VSCode either. Error in runtime: 'Unexpected token export'. Editor: 'Could not find a declaration file for module "@redwood/inference"'. Anyone seen this?

owen: Can you paste package.json `exports` + tsconfig you're using?

maya: Sure, here's the minimal repro from the app: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
and tsconfig has `module: esnext`, `target: es2020`.

zara: Edge runtime (Workers) expects ESM and doesn't like any CJS remnants. The 'Unexpected token export' usually means a file with `export` was delivered to an environment that tried to parse it as CJS (or the bundler emitted an ESM file but Workers got something else).

zara: Also VSCode resolution: if `types` is only inside `exports["."]` some older TS versions / editors don't resolve it unless there's a top-level `types` field. Do we have that?

maya: We don't. We assumed types inside exports would be enough. Editor error goes away if I add "types": "dist/index.d.ts" at root package.json. But runtime still fails.

raj: Related question: are we seeing auth/retry differences between builds? I remember someone mentioning fetch-based runtimes skip our axios-style interceptors.

maya: Yes — in the edge sample the token refresh path doesn't trigger on 401. The SDK's retry middleware is designed for Node (uses `node-fetch` wrapper + re-invoke request), but our ESM edge bundle ends up using a tiny fetch wrapper that doesn't re-run middleware chain. So auth refresh + retry doesn't happen. Repro: login -> token expires -> request 401 -> app shows auth failure instead of refreshing.

owen: Short term workaround: bundle with a wrapper that exposes `sdkRequest` which will re-run the token refresh flow, or polyfill the retry behavior in the app. Long term: SDK should provide a fetch-friendly retry hook for edge consumers.

owen: Also note: for Workers you must bundle with esbuild `format: 'esm'` and target `es2020`/`es2022` — and avoid outputting `require()` calls.

maya: Here's the console trace in the worker: 
```
TypeError: Unexpected token 'export'
 at file:///usr/src/app/dist/esm/utils.js:1:1
 at file:///usr/src/app/dist/esm/index.js:2:3
```

zara: Filed a small DX bug for the typings+exports mismatch: https://redwood-internal/bugs/4287 :eyes:

sam-devx: Thanks for the repro, @maya. We'll do three things: 1) docs note about `types` at package root + `exports` caveat, 2) add an Edge sample-app doc (esbuild config snippet + recommended bundle flags), 3) create a small SDK change to expose a fetch-compatible retry hook. I'll add a smoke e2e for Workers so CI catches regressions. ETA EOD tomorrow. :rocket:

maya: I'll open a PR for the sample-app with the esbuild config and the failing repro. cc @owen for the retry hook design.

owen: Happy to pair on the hook. Suggest API: `client = new RedwoodClient({ fetchImpl?: typeof fetch, retryHandler?: (req, res) => Promise<boolean> })` so edge apps can pass globalThis.fetch and a custom retry handler.

raj: That API sounds safe. We should default preserve current behavior for Node.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Sample-app worker test failed on canary — 1 failing test (auth-retry-edge-smoke).

sam-devx: Noted — I'll queue the fix and add a CI job to run the worker smoke using `wrangler dev` style harness.

maya: Thanks all — saved me hours. I'll send the PR in ~30m. :thumbsup:
